standard_prerequisites.name: There are no maps from A_f to a module derived complete with respect to f
standard_prerequisites.use: Forces the constructed localization map to vanish, giving y_n = 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of derived completeness with respect to f and the module M' as the kernel of the map to the f-adic completion
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the objects and the meaning of the conclusion JM' = 0.

standard_prerequisites.name: Divisibility of elements of M' by arbitrary powers of f
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the sequences x_n and hence the elements y_n.

core_obligations: Take x in M' and g in J, write x = f^n x_n for every n >= 1, and use that g lies in f^nA to conclude that y_n = g x_n is independent of the choice of x_n (proof lines 27075-27077).
Take x_n = f x_{n+1} to obtain y_n = f y_{n+1}, and conclude that there is a map A_f -> M sending 1/f^n to y_n (proof lines 27078-27079).
Invoke the statement that there are no maps from A_f to a derived complete module to conclude this map is zero, hence y_n = 0 for all n (proof lines 27080-27081).
Conclude gx = g f x_1 = f y_1 = 0, which proves JM' = 0 and, when A is derived complete, that J has square zero (proof lines 27082-27083).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an element f of a ring A, sets J equal to the intersection of the ideals f^nA, and lets M be an A-module derived complete with respect to f; it asserts that JM' = 0, where M' is the kernel of M -> lim M/f^nM, and in particular that if A is derived complete then J is an ideal of square zero (source lines 27066-27072). The proof is a direct element chase. Take x in M' and g in J; for every n >= 1 one may write x = f^n x_n, and since g lies in f^nA the element y_n = g x_n of M' is independent of the choice of x_n (proof lines 27075-27077). One may therefore take x_n = f x_{n+1}, which yields y_n = f y_{n+1}; this compatible system defines a map A_f -> M sending 1/f^n to y_n (proof lines 27078-27079). The author then invokes the derived completeness of M in the form of the statement that there are no maps from A_f to a derived complete module, so that this map must be zero and hence every y_n vanishes (proof lines 27080-27081). Finally gx = g f x_1 = f y_1 = 0, completing the proof (proof lines 27082-27083). The non-routine content is the construction of the compatible family y_n and the recognition that the derived completeness of M forces the resulting localization map to vanish.
